verbalization: Nifurpirinol is implicated in the interaction with ZR-75-1 through a multi-step mechanism involving the G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2 protein. This protein serves as a target for both Isocurcumenol and trans-urocanic acid, which are secondary targets of Nifurpirinol. The evidence suggests that Nifurpirinol modulates the activity of the G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2, which in turn affects the function of ZR-75-1. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential role for Nifurpirinol in influencing cellular signaling through the G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2, ultimately impacting ZR-75-1. The relationship is supported by the sequential targeting of the G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2 by two distinct compounds, indicating a possible regulatory role for Nifurpirinol in this signaling cascade.
